title: Phase 0's expected-value literal is hardcoded into a control the runbook presents as a manual human check, and is both stale and structurally incomplete
fingerprintNote: Carried VERBATIM from classified-findings.json; not recomputed by finding-manager.
description: story-072 checklist line 1195 — one of only two unticked items and, alongside line 1197, the entire compensating human control — instructs the operator to confirm 'the new pooler holds the full 16,338.8190 BPT' and 'the rescued ~349 USDC sits in the streamer buffer'. Both figures are stale. This audit's live :dry run measured 16,867.5264 BPT (16867526417628291567945 wei) and a final stream buffer of 530.761796 USDC (99.224124 from the old batch minter + 51.537672 UniboostSCX residual prime + 380.000000 from DelayRelease). The CODE is unaffected — Phase 0 derives the baseline live (side-effects.json confirms bptAtPhase0 == the live figure) and no assertion references the stale number; the 16,338.819e18 literal survives only as a self-contained fixture in test/BptBaselinePersistence.t.sol:96. The defect is confined to the manual control.
impact: None directly — and this is load-bearing for the grade. The CODE is unaffected: Phase 0 derives the BPT baseline live (bptAtPhase0 == the measured 16867526417628291567945), no assertion references the stale literal, and the 16,338.819e18 figure survives only as a self-contained fixture in test/BptBaselinePersistence.t.sol:96. The degraded asset is a COMPENSATING HUMAN CONTROL: story-072 checklist line 1195, one of the two unticked rows, and the row the operator is meant to use for the post-cutover state that :verify cannot mechanise.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. The operator completes the broadcast and turns to checklist line 1195 to confirm the end state by hand.
2. Line 1195 says 'the new pooler holds the full 16,338.8190 BPT'. The live measurement is 16,867.5264 BPT. Mismatch #1.

3. Line 1195 says 'the rescued ~349 USDC (98.04 + 250.77)' sits in the streamer buffer. The measured buffer is 530.761796 USDC, and it decomposes as 99.224124 (old batch minter) + 380.000000 (DelayRelease) + 51.537672 (UniboostSCX residual prime) — a THIRD component the checklist never names at all. Mismatch #2, and it is structural, not arithmetic: the control does not know what it is counting.

4a. Benign branch: the operator treats the mismatch as a real failure and raises an alarm on a healthy cutover. Because line 1195 is a POST-broadcast row, this causes confusion and delay, not a partial application.

4b. Dangerous branch: the operator reconciles the mismatch as 'the checklist numbers are always a bit off', and the control is now calibrated to be waved through — so a GENUINE BPT shortfall or a missing buffer component on the day reads exactly like the noise they have been trained to ignore.

5. The BPT half of line 1195 is partially backstopped: :verify consumes story-074's persisted baseline and re-runs the Phase 7 conservation assertion. The USDC-buffer half is NOT backstopped by anything — and that is precisely the half whose decomposition is structurally incomplete.
likelihood: certain to trigger (every quoted figure mismatches at cutover time), but the harmful branch (4b) requires the coincidence of operator numbness AND an independent real failure.
assumptions: The operator actually performs line 1195 — it is currently unticked, so this is not guaranteed either way.
externalRequirements: For material harm, an independent genuine shortfall must occur at the same time as the numbness. Alone, this finding causes only a false alarm.
evidence: side-effects.json -> leadsResolution[3], preconditionResults (bptAtPhase0 = 16867526417628291567945), stateWrites (USDC breakdown 99224124 + 51537672 + 380000000 = 530761796). Log: scratchpad/dry.log:117-124, :156, :184-185, :199.
justification: Ratified at Low, having re-weighed it as structurally incomplete rather than merely stale — the deduplicator is right that this strengthens the finding, and it is reflected in the write-up rather than in the number. This is a Law-3 footgun and it is in scope: a competent, non-malicious operator would be surprised to find every figure in a control they were told to rely on mismatching, and the surprise pushes in a dangerous direction. It is NOT reckless-admin noise and NOT a documentation carve-out — the 'documentation/style' exclusion covers NatSpec, formatting and pragmas, whereas here the degraded artefact IS the control. But the honest ceiling is Low. The code is correct and derives everything live; the primary quantity (BPT) is independently re-checked by :verify against a write-once persisted baseline; and material harm needs a compounding conditional — numbness AND a simultaneous real shortfall. The false-alarm direction, which is the branch certain to occur, cannot leave a partially-applied cutover because line 1195 is post-broadcast: by the time the operator reads it, everything has already landed. Medium would require a function or availability impact this cannot produce on its own, so Medium would be overstatement.
recommendation: Stop hardcoding balances in the human checklist. Rewrite line 1195 to say: 'confirm the new pooler's BPT equals the `BPT cutover baseline` printed by Phase 0 of the immediately preceding `:dry` run, and the streamer buffer equals its final `collectNudge -> stream buffer now` figure' — the script already prints both, under a '--- stranded value (live) ---' header built for exactly this purpose. Additionally, have `_printSummary()` emit a copy-paste 'POST-BROADCAST HUMAN CHECKLIST' block with the live-derived expected values filled in, so the operator compares against measurements taken minutes earlier rather than against prose written weeks earlier. When rewriting, enumerate ALL THREE buffer components (old batch minter / DelayRelease / UniboostSCX residual prime) or, better, quote only the total the script prints — a control that names two of three sources will drift again the moment a fourth donor appears.

specConformance.criterion: checklist line 1195 — post-broadcast human check: on-chain confirmation of the whole end state.
specConformance.state: UNTICKED, and its stated expected values are factually wrong against live mainnet at c4396b1 (16,338.8190 vs 16,867.5264 BPT; ~349 USDC vs 530.761796 USDC across three components, one unnamed).
specConformance.deviation: The story asserts an end state that does not match the state its own suite produces. This is a deviation in the story text itself, not in the implementation — the code is faithful; the acceptance criterion is not accurate.

collapseRefusalCarried: F-01 and F-05 share the story-072 checklist as an artefact but were confirmed distinct by the deduplicator: enforceable-but-unenforced (fails silent) versus stated-but-wrong (fails noisy, then numb), with non-overlapping fixes in both directions. Kept separate here.
